title: Priority-aware shedding telemetry playground and failover dashboard
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement telemetry and dashboards to validate priority-aware load shedding, multi-region failover behavior, and circuit-breaker triggers at token-level granularity. This ticket builds an instrumentation playground and a set of Grafana dashboards and alerts to help engineers tune SLO thresholds and shedding policies before rollout.
context: We have numerous SLI workstreams for token-level latency and regional failover, but lack a focused environment to validate priority-based shedding: requests assigned priority classes (system, paid, free) should see predictable latency degradation and graceful failover. Existing dashboards show per-route p95/p99 but not tokenized histograms, admission vs served counts, or model-variant fallback traces. This makes it hard to calibrate circuit thresholds and rolling policies.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument request path to emit token-level latency histograms with tags: region, shard_id, priority_class, route, model_variant, cause (cache_hit|admit|evict|shed).
Expose admit_rate, admit_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, per-priority drop_rate as metrics fed to metrics pipeline.

Create Grafana dashboard 'Priority Shed Playground' with: (1) token-latency heatmap by priority and region; (2) admission queue depth and per-shard concurrency; (3) circuit state timeline and triggered fallbacks; (4) synthetic traffic control panel to toggle priority mixes.
Implement alerting rules for unexpected admission drop spikes (>2x baseline) and circuit open duration > 1m for >10% of shards.
Run chaos experiment: with synthetic high free-tier traffic, confirm paid-tier tail p99 remains < latency SLO degradation budget and document thresholds.
technical_notes: Metric names: inference.token_latency_ms (histogram), inference.token_admit_rate (gauge), inference.token_admit_count (counter), inference.kv_hit_ratio (gauge), inference.circuit_state (enum). Use OpenMetrics labels for tags.
Histogram buckets: exponential from 0.5ms to 2000ms with finer buckets around 10ms-200ms for GPU serving.
Telemetry path: agent -> metrics-proxy -> prom-remotewrite -> metrics warehouse (Mimir) -> grafana. Use batching to avoid amplification.
Add lightweight trace spans: shard_decision, admit_decision, kv_lookup, model_invoke, fallback_route. Correlate with token index for heavy tail analysis.
Prefer sampling for traces: sample 100% for circuits open events and 1% for baseline requests.
Store compact token SLI rollups (p50/p95/p99 per-minute per-shard) to avoid cardinality explosion.
rollout_plan: 1) Instrumentation feature flag behind 'priority_shed_telemetry' in runtime config.
2) Deploy to canary region with internal traffic split (5% prod ingress with synthetic mix).
3) Validate dashboards and alerts, iterate thresholds.
4) Expand to 25% ingress and run targeted chaos tests.
5) Full rollout with scheduled monitoring window and postmortem checklist.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric emission and label correctness.
Integration test in staging that pumps synthetic mixed-priority traffic and verifies metric ingestion and dashboard panels update within 60s.
Chaos test: simulate shard loss and validate failover metrics show fallback_model_invocations increase and paid priority latency preserved.
SLI regression test using long-running load harness to assert p99 budgets by priority.
